title: Capstone Project I: Architecture & Fleet Dispatch

why-capstone-architecture.title: The Martian Capstone Mission
why-capstone-architecture.content:
### The Grand Fleet Deployment

All systems are primed. The entire IRIS autonomous exploration squadron — **Scout Drone Sigma**, **Survey Drone Delta**, and **Heavy Drone Omega** — stands on the launch terraces overlooking the vast canyon of Valles Marineris.

Over the past 30 chapters, you mastered every foundational element of modern C++:
- Data types, variables, arithmetic, and conditional logic
- Loops, standard algorithms, and arrays (1D & 2D)
- Dynamic memory collections with `std::vector`
- Modular function design, references, and parameter passing
- Strings (`std::string`), output formatting (`<iomanip>`), and structures (`struct`)
- Stream I/O, file storage (`<fstream>`), and defensive input validation

Now, in this two-part **Capstone Project (Chapters 31 & 32)**, you will unite these separate techniques into an industrial-grade autonomous mission control architecture.

In **Phase I (Chapter 31)**, you will design the core data models, flight readiness validators, waypoint energy dispatchers, and formatted squadron telemetry reporting.

In **Phase II (Chapter 32)**, you will execute the full autonomous mission simulation, terrain navigation, and emergency flight blackbox recording!

capstone-system-architecture.title: Modular Avionics Architecture
capstone-system-architecture.content:
### Software Design of the Fleet Controller

A robust space software architecture divides responsibilities into distinct modular layers:

![Capstone System Architecture](assets/l31-final1-architecture.en.svg)

#### 1. Data Models (`struct`)
Clean definitions representing real-world entities:
- `struct Drone`: identity, name, battery level, current altitude.
- `struct Waypoint`: navigational coordinates `(x, y)`.

#### 2. Logic & Validation Functions
Modular routines passed by constant reference (`const &`) for zero-copy safety:
- `bool is_launch_ready(const Drone &d)`: ensures minimum 50% battery and non-negative altitude.
- `int step_cost(const Waypoint &from, const Waypoint &to)`: calculates energy consumed between coordinates.

#### 3. Storage & Presentation Engine
- `std::vector<Drone>` manages dynamic squadron rosters.
- `<iomanip>` (`left`, `right`, `setw`, `setprecision`) renders crystal-clear mission control displays.

write-capstone-drone-model.title: Avionics Logic: Launch Readiness Gate
write-capstone-drone-model.content:
### Fleet Qualification Gatekeeper

Define the flight qualification function `is_launch_ready`.

A drone is qualified for launch if and only if:
1. `d.battery >= 50`
2. `d.altitude >= 0`

Input format:
Four tokens on one line: `int id`, `string name`, `int battery`, `int altitude`.

Output format:
`LAUNCH READY: 1` (if ready) or `LAUNCH READY: 0` (if not ready).
write-capstone-drone-model.task:
1. Define function `bool is_launch_ready(const Drone &d)` that returns `true` if `battery >= 50 && altitude >= 0`, and `false` otherwise.
2. In `main()`, call `is_launch_ready(d)`.
3. Output `LAUNCH READY: <1 or 0>` followed by a newline.

write-capstone-waypoint-dispatcher.title: Navigation Engine: Waypoint Battery Dispatcher
write-capstone-waypoint-dispatcher.content:
### Energy Trajectory Simulation

Scout Drone Sigma starts at coordinate `(0, 0)` with a known battery level.

Input:
1. Two integers: `battery` and `n` (number of waypoints).
2. `n` pairs of integers representing `x` and `y` coordinates.

Rules:
- Movement cost from `(cur_x, cur_y)` to `(x, y)` is `abs(x - cur_x) + abs(y - cur_y)`.
- Deduct movement cost from `battery`.
- If `battery` drops below 0, clamp it to 0.
- Update current coordinates to `(x, y)`.

Output:
`FINAL BATTERY: <battery>`
write-capstone-waypoint-dispatcher.task:
1. In `main()`, read `battery` and `n`.
2. Initialize `cur_x = 0` and `cur_y = 0`.
3. Loop `n` times reading `x` and `y`.
4. Subtract Manhattan distance `abs(x - cur_x) + abs(y - cur_y)` from `battery`.
5. If `battery < 0`, set `battery = 0`.
6. Output `FINAL BATTERY: <battery>` followed by a newline.

capstone-stage1-fleet-director.title: Capstone Phase I: Fleet Readiness Director
capstone-stage1-fleet-director.content:
### Squadron Flight Deck Controller

Implement the Phase I Fleet Director program.

Input format:
1. Integer `n` (number of drones in squadron).
2. `n` lines, each containing:
   `int id`, `string name`, `int battery`, `int altitude`.

Processing:
- Store all drones in `vector<Drone> fleet`.
- Count how many drones are launch ready (`battery >= 50 && altitude >= 0`).
- Calculate the average battery percentage across all `n` drones.

Output format:
1. Formatted table header:
   `DRONE        BATTERY  ALTITUDE`
   (Columns: name left-aligned width 8, battery right-aligned width 10, altitude right-aligned width 10).
2. For each drone, output its row using identical alignment and widths.
3. Output `FLEET READY: <ready_count>`.
4. Output `AVG BATTERY: <fixed << setprecision(1) << avg>`.
capstone-stage1-fleet-director.task:
1. Read integer `n` and populate `vector<Drone> fleet`.
2. Print the table header using `left << setw(8) << "DRONE" << right << setw(10) << "BATTERY" << setw(10) << "ALTITUDE"`.
3. Loop over `fleet` and print each drone row using identical widths.
4. Count drones satisfying `battery >= 50 && altitude >= 0` and print `FLEET READY: <count>`.
5. Calculate average battery and print `AVG BATTERY: <fixed << setprecision(1) << avg>`.

recap.title: Summary: Capstone Phase I Accomplished
recap.content:
### Capstone Architecture Ready for Launch

You have constructed the modular backbone of the IRIS mission control software!

#### Phase I Architecture Summary

| Layer | Module | Responsibilities |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Model** | `struct Drone` | Encapsulates ID, name, battery %, and altitude |
| **Model** | `struct Waypoint` | Navigational coordinates `(x, y)` |
| **Logic** | `is_launch_ready()` | Constant reference pass-by-ref (`const &`) qualification |
| **Logic** | `step_cost()` | Energy projection via Manhattan metric |
| **Presentation** | `<iomanip>` Table | Formatted telemetry board with aligned fields |
| **Analytics** | Metrics Aggregator | Fleet-wide readiness counters and battery averages |

> [!NOTE]
> Modular separation allows each component to be tested and verified independently — the fundamental standard of mission-critical aerospace software.

Next in Chapter 32: **Capstone Project II (Grand Finale)** — full autonomous canyon expedition, blackbox logging, flight simulation, and course graduation!
